FSD v1.1 is fundamentally sound; §4.2 (M-01..M-08) already marks code gaps as TO-BE, so those need NO FSD fix — DEV implements per TDD §11.1. The 6 items below are places where FSD wording is inaccurate, undecided, or silent and BA should amend FSD (SA did NOT modify FSD).

## Discrepancies

### DISC-01: Anthropic "one API call per array" vs per-text API reality [Medium]
- **FSD says:** §3.4.5.1 + §6.4 + NFR-01 — `countTokens` is "1 API call per array" for all providers, including Anthropic (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` with "full batch").
- **Actuality:** Anthropic `count_tokens` accepts ONE text per request (per-text `messages` + `input_tokens` response). A batched method call necessarily fans out to N sequential HTTP sub-calls.
- **Impact:** NFR-01 ("exactly 1 API call") is untestable for Anthropic; DEV estimate and QA batch test (TC-08) need the qualified definition.
- **Recommended fix:** BA amends §3.4.5.1/NFR-01 to "1 LOGICAL batched call per array (Anthropic executes per-text sub-calls internally; order/length guarantee unchanged)". TDD records this as decision D-08 (§3.3, §5.3).

### DISC-02: OpenAI-cloud count strategy undecided (OI-03) [Medium]
- **FSD says:** §5.2 offers two options (tiktoken WASM vs `chat/completions` dry-run `usage`) and assigns the decision to SA/TDD draft.
- **Actuality:** Decision required before DEV estimate; FSD cannot stay undecided.
- **Impact:** Blocks implementation of the cloud path.
- **Recommended fix:** BA records SA decision D-01 in §5.2: cloud path uses `js-tiktoken` (NEW DEPENDENCY, offline/sync/no token cost); dry-run alternative explicitly rejected with rationale (TDD §5.3).

### DISC-03: smollm2 window 1024 vs 2048 without enforced-denominator ruling (M-03) [Low]
- **FSD says:** §3.1.1 + §3.4.5.3 seed registry `1024`; §4.2 M-03 notes `ONNX_MODEL_REGISTRY` has `2048` and asks TDD to "record the decision" — but §3.1.1 presents `1024` as settled fact.
- **Actuality:** Two live values for the same model; gate denominator ambiguous until ruled.
- **Impact:** Low (fail-safe either way), but QA golden fixtures must pin one value.
- **Recommended fix:** BA adds ruling note to §3.1.1: enforced denominator `1024` (fail-safe); ONNX `2048` is physical-max only. TDD decision D-02 (§4.3).

### DISC-04: Legacy `langgraph/core/context-budget.ts` fail-open path outside FSD scope [Medium]
- **FSD says:** BR-07 — `contextWindow = 0` means unknown → usage treated as 100% (fail-closed).
- **Actual codebase:** `langgraph/core/context-budget.ts:218-220` `checkAutoCompact` returns `{ shouldCompact: false, usagePercent: 0 }` when `contextBudget <= 0` — fail-OPEN, contradicting BR-07 if read as applying to all budget code. FSD never names this legacy function or scopes BR-07 to the Pi gate.
- **Impact:** DEV might "fix" the legacy path (scope creep) or QA might assert BR-07 against it (false failure).
- **Recommended fix:** BA adds scope note to BR-07/§6: "BR-07 applies to the Pi pre-session gate (`pi-agent/context-budget.ts`) only; `langgraph/core` legacy pruning is out of scope for SA4E-324 (separate ticket)". TDD §1.2 + D-09 already scope it out.

### DISC-05: NFR-01 batch definition vs Ollama apportioned dry-run [Low]
- **FSD says:** NFR-01 — "exactly 1 API call per array (no N calls)".
- **Actuality:** Ollama fallback strategy (§5.3) is ONE `/api/chat` dry-run with apportioned counts — 1 call but approximate (flagged `conservative=true`), which NFR-01's timing/count assertions don't distinguish from exact counts.
- **Impact:** QA batch test could assert exactness where only approximation is guaranteed.
- **Recommended fix:** BA qualifies NFR-01: "1 logical call per array; Ollama dry-run apportionment is approximate and MUST set `conservative=true`". TDD §3.3 + §5.3 specify this.

### DISC-06: Registry-vs-catalog "ID-consistent" rule overstates reality [Low]
- **FSD says:** §3.1.1 — "`chat-models.ts` static catalog ... must stay ID-consistent with the registry".
- **Actual codebase:** registry has 9 IDs; `chat-models.ts` catalog has 40+ IDs across 7 providers (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8`, `o1`, `deepseek-v3-2`) with no registry entries and different purposes (dropdown fallback vs budget denominator).
- **Impact:** Read literally, every catalog ID needs a registry entry — unintended scope expansion.
- **Recommended fix:** BA clarifies §3.1.1: IDs SHARED between catalog and registry (phi-3-mini, smollm2-360m, llama3.1, qwen2.5-coder, local-model, gpt-4o/mini, claude-3/opus) must match exactly; catalog-only IDs are out of budget-gate scope (unknown model → default fallback per BR-04).
